summary: Yakupitiyage Karunadasa worked in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied at the University of Ceylon and earned his Ph.D. at the University of London under David Friedman. He served as Director of the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies (~1980–2000).
Yan Fu was a scholar of philosophy and sinology who studied at the Royal Naval College (~1877–1879). He later held posts at Fudan University (~1905–1907) and Peking University (~1912).
Yanfei Zhou specializes in Buddhist studies, history, archaeology, and sinology. Zhou completed a PhD at the National University of Singapore under the supervision of Yuet Keung Lo.

Yang Wenhui was a scholar in Buddhist studies and sinology. He founded the Jinling Scriptural Press in 1897, the Zhiheng Jingshe and Jetavana Hermitage in 1908, and the Buddhist Research Society in 1910, serving as its head.
Yang-Gyu An is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. An studied under Hojin and earned a D.Phil. at the University of Oxford by 1998 under Richard Gombrich.
Yangdon Dhondup works in Tibetology. Dhondup earned a PhD at SOAS University of London under the supervision of Henry Y. H. Zhao.
Yanling Chen works in Buddhist studies. Chen earned a Master of Arts at Fo Guang University (attested 2012) under the supervision of Yongdong Shi and studied under traditional teacher Hsing Yun.
Yannick Laurent specializes in Tibetology, history, and archaeology. Laurent holds posts at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities and the University of Munich (both attested 2026).
Yanpei was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Taixu (~1934–1939) and Yinshun (~1941–1945).
Yao Wang was a Tibetologist who studied under traditional teacher Gongkar Tulku. Wang later served as a guest professor at the University of Vienna.
Yao-ming Tsai specializes in Buddhist studies and philosophy. After earning a PhD from the University of California by 1997, Tsai became Professor of Philosophy at National Taiwan University.
Yaping Dou is a scholar of Buddhist studies and religious studies who earned a PhD at The Chinese University of Hong Kong under the supervision of Xue Yu (attested 2010).

Yaroslav Komarovski is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at several Tibetan institutes and the University of Virginia, later holding posts at Washington University in St. Louis and the University of Nebraska-Lincoln (attested 2011–2015).

Yaroslav Vasilkov specializes in Indology. He studied at the Faculty of Oriental Studies of St. Petersburg University (~1961–1966) and held posts at Saint Petersburg State University (~1968) and the Russian Academy of Sciences (~1978).

Yasuaki Nara was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at the University of Tokyo under Hajime Nakamura and at the University of Calcutta. He held appointments at Komazawa University and served as director of the Soto Zen Research Center.

Yasuhiko Nagano is a scholar of Tibetology and linguistics. After earning a Ph.D. at UC Berkeley (~1976–1983), he held posts at UC Berkeley, the National Museum of Ethnology, the National Institutes for the Humanities, and the Graduate University for Advanced Studies.
Yasuhiko Sueki is a scholar of sinology and philosophy. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1972–1980) and held the title of professor emeritus at Komazawa University (~2018).

Yasuhiro Okazaki works in Indology and philosophy. Okazaki completed a PhD at Hiroshima University under Atsushi Uno, Shoryu Katsura, and Hiroakira Ono, and later held teaching positions at Chiyoda, Kabe, and Hiroshima Prefectural Takamiya high schools.

Yasuhiro Sueki is a Buddhist studies scholar who undertook short-term study under George Baumann at Tübingen University Library (~1983–1984). He held posts at the International Institute for Buddhist Studies and the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies.

Yasuhiro Tsuchiyama is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies who is attested as a lecturer at both the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies in 2026.
